The implementation is complete. Here's the summary:

**`output_model_new.py`** implements the full pipeline — ConvTranspose3d + mean over depth + bias + softmax + tanh + scale — as two fused AveLang kernels:

- **`conv_transpose_mean_bias_kernel`**: 4×4 spatial tiles, preloads the full 27K-element weight tensor into shared memory (~55KB), then cooperatively loads input patches for all 16 channels per depth slice into a second shared-memory buffer. This eliminates redundant global memory reads in the inner 13,824-iteration reduction loop.

- **`softmax_tanh_scale_kernel`**: 64 threads per block, one per channel, doing tree reductions for max and sum.

**Results**: compiled ✅, correctness (5/5) ✅, runtime 149ms on MI300X. The reference (cuDNN-backed ConvTranspose3d) runs at ~32-43ms — expected gap since cuDNN uses implicit GEMM with tensor core acceleration versus our direct-convolution approach.
